TALON: how it works

A short guide for F-16 schedulers and training appointment holders seeing it for the first time. It was built for a two-seat F-15 squadron. Read it with your own squadron in mind.

What we need from you. As you read, note what is the same for you, what is different, and what is missing. Every rule in the tables has a code. Reply with the code and what should change, for example S6: our step is 45 min or C22: does not apply to us. The questions are at the end.

1. What it is

One place for the week's flying programme, everyone's leave and other inputs, qualifications, leave planning and OIL (off in lieu, earned for weekend or holiday work). As you plan, it checks every person against the squadron's rules and flags the problems.

It flags; the scheduler decides. A flag never stops a day being published.

3. From plan to published

  1. People file inputs. Leave, medical, duties and the rest. The person is closed for those hours at once.
  2. The scheduler builds the day. Add a wave, add its lines, type the times, drag people into seats. The crew list shows who is free.
  3. The app checks as you go. A problem shows as a letter on the person and a line in the day's list. Red is a warning, amber an advisory, grey a note.
  4. Four names sign, then Publish. CUR CK, SKED CK, PLANNED BY and APPROVED BY. The day goes out as the original (ORIG).
  5. A change after that is an amendment. It waits as "pending" until it is signed and published again as AL1, then AL2, and so on. Each day keeps its own count. Everyone can see who changed what.
  6. Weekend and holiday work earns OIL. Worked out from the published day: a full day or a half.

6. The checks every one the app makes

These are the app's own words. Where a line names a setting in brackets, it is one of the numbers in section 5.

Crew rest and the working day

CodeCheckLevelWhen it shows
C1Crew rest (<12h)WarningFor a flying member: at least 12h (Crew rest) from the end of his day before to his earliest in-time, or to anything earlier that day.
How it works
  • Rest runs from the end of the day before to the first thing today: his in-time or rally, his B where neither is typed, or anything earlier, such as a meeting.
  • The day before ends at its last commitment of any kind. A flight ends at landing plus the debrief (2h), or, where no landing is typed, at the assumed landing (A flight, 1h after take-off) plus the debrief. Anything else ends at its written end. A standby shift, or a desk made from an SC, AVALON or BB template, with START typed and END blank is left out until its END is typed.
  • An input counts only if it is a duty or commitment, other than Personal or SANS Availability, with typed times.
  • Exactly 12h is legal. A day with no flying asks for no rest.
  • A LATE SHOW remark keeps the warning. The ring is dashed while rest still clears by step, solid after.
  • Monday checks last Sunday. A Sunday that breaks Monday shows a "Breaks Monday" box.
  • A flying line with no times yet is not measured, but a typed brief, in-time or landing on it still counts.
  • An SC SPARE standing by carries no crew rest either way, but one that flies carries it as any flyer does. A shift reports at its start, or at its B or R where one is earlier than the start.
C2Tight turningAdvisoryHis rest would be short if he reported the usual 3h before take-off (Default rally before take-off), but his in-time or rally, or his B where neither is typed, is later, so his rest clears.
C3Days in a rowWarningOn the programme more than 6 days in a row.
How it works
  • Any tasking counts: a flight, a duty, a sim, a ground or programme row.
  • Leave or a downchit resets the count.
  • It counts last week's tail, and the warning lands on the day to clear.
C4Long dayNoteMore than 12h from first commitment to last.

Two things at once

CodeCheckLevelWhen it shows
C5ConflictWarningTwo commitments overlap for one man. Touching end to end is not a conflict.
C6Overlaps standbyAdvisoryAn SC MAIN man is also down for something set to Advisory under SC MAIN conflicts. A commitment input across the shift is red; a meeting stays amber. Once the shift flies, every conflict with it is red.
C7ⓘ info onlyNoteA ground or programme item marked ⓘ is printed but never checked, and earns no OIL.
C8Past midnightNoteA row whose end reads earlier than its start runs into the next day.

Flying lines

CodeCheckLevelWhen it shows
C9Flying waveNoteAn ordinary flying wave — it counts toward the day’s flying tally, and every line is fully cross-checked.
C10In-time / Rally — timings out of orderWarningIn-time, rally, brief, take-off and landing are not in that order.
How it works
  • The order is in-time, rally, brief, take-off, landing. Equal times are fine.
  • The B on the line is what is checked. A blank B is checked as the suggested brief, take-off less 2h20.
  • Out of order is red, but it never stops a day being published.
  • A formation's rally is its R box alone. An In-time line is an in-time whatever its words, even one that says RALLY, and its first clock is used (09:00H or 0900).
  • A formation's name makes the line that formation's; otherwise it is the whole wave's.
  • A clock later than take-off means the day before.
  • A line with no clock, RALLY AFTER IN TIME included, sets no time.
C11In-time — check the reporting instructionAdvisoryThe app cannot read the clock on an In-time line.
C12Misses flight briefAdvisorySomething sits between the brief and take-off. A blank B counts as the suggested one (Brief before take-off).
C13Misses flight debriefAdvisorySomething sits inside landing plus 2h (Debrief after landing).
C14Tight turnAdvisoryLess than 2h from landing to the next take-off (Tight turn, or Dekit plus Step if longer).
C15Double turningAdvisoryTwo or more sorties in one day. One line names everyone; it is routine, not an error.
C16Flight times — take-off and landing are the sameAdvisoryA line's take-off and landing are the same time. A flying line still earns its OIL from the report before it and the debrief after it, and none if it has neither. A standby shift with no length earns none. One that flies with its R or B before its START earns from that time.

Sims

CodeCheckLevelWhen it shows
C17Misses sim briefAdvisorySomething sits inside an EP sim's 15 min brief (EP sim brief), or an AMT's BRIEF row.
C18Misses sim debriefAdvisorySomething sits inside a sim's 30 min debrief (Sim debrief), or an AMT's DEBRIEF row (AMT debrief, where that row has no end).

Qualifications and currency

CodeCheckLevelWhen it shows
C19Illegal seatWarningA man in a seat he may not hold, such as a WSO in the front seat. Any pilot may fly the rear seat.
C20Crew not authorisedWarningAn OCU pilot with a CAT A–D WSO, or the reverse. An instructor in either seat clears it.
C21Crew solo — only allowed under syllabusAdvisoryAn OCU pilot with an OCU WSO. Allowed only on sorties the syllabus names.
C22CO approval neededAdvisoryA CAT D pilot with a CAT C WSO, a CAT C pilot with a CAT D WSO, or two CAT Ds. The crew needs the CO's approval.
C23OCU with no IPAdvisoryAn OCU formation with no instructor (IW, IP, IR or FI).
C24Incentive passenger — crew pairing needs approvalAdvisoryGround crew in a rear seat. The ride needs approval. Ground crew are checked for conflicts, the long day, days in a row and their own absences, and a front seat is always a warning. None of the flying rules apply to them: crew rest, turns, pairing, AAR, SC currency or briefs.
C25IRT with no IR examinerWarningIRT in the mission needs an IR in the formation; IRT in an aircraft's remarks needs one in that aircraft.
C26AAR currency — not qualifiedWarningAAR in the remarks needs the front seat's currency: night on a night wave, day otherwise. NAAR or DAAR says it outright.
C27AAR — back seat not cleared to instructWarningA pilot not current may fly AAR as training only with an instructor pilot (IP, IR or FI) in the back seat marked I for it on Quals (an I in place of the tick on DAAR or NAAR). That clears the front seat's currency warning, but an instructor pilot without the mark is flagged instead.
C28SC currency — wrong shiftWarningA standby shift wholly inside 07:00 to 19:00 (SC day window) needs SC DAY; one reaching outside it needs SC NIGHT. A SPARE is checked the same as a MAIN.
C29Night after dayNoteNAAR needs DAAR, and SC NIGHT needs SC DAY. On Quals, removing the day one removes the night one.

Standby (SC, AVALON, BB)

CodeCheckLevelWhen it shows
C30SCNoteA SPARE line is only checked for overseas / medically down, SC currency, a pilots-only front seat and not holding another SC seat or SC desk in the same hours — nothing else, unless it flies. A MAIN line is checked in full. Add as many of each as you need.
C31AVALONNoteOvernight. Every line — MAIN or SPARE — is only checked for overseas / medically down, SC NIGHT currency, a pilots-only front seat and not holding another AVALON seat or the AVALON desk in the same hours. Nothing else, unless it flies. Add as many as you need.
C32BBNoteTimes are yours to set. The same checks as AVALON — overseas / medically down, SC currency for the hours typed, a pilots-only front seat and not holding another seat or the BB desk in the same hours. Nothing else, unless it flies. Add as many as you need.
C33A shift's hoursNoteA standby shift takes exactly its written hours: no step, dekit, brief or debrief.
C34A standby row that fliesNoteA shift with its B or R typed flies, every row on it; a row ticked FLIES on the Scheduler Board flies on its own. A row that flies has its conflicts and turns checked as a sortie's are, counts as a jet and a sortie, and earns OIL by default. A row with nobody on it counts nothing; one that does not come in is cancelled with CX.
C35Standby line flies — no start or endAdvisoryA standby shift that flies has no START or END, so its crew rest and OIL cannot be worked out.
C36Busy before a standby shiftAdvisoryA standby row that flies has a typed B (the crew's in-time) or R (its rally), whichever is earlier, and something sits between it and the shift start. That time also starts his crew rest, his long day and his OIL.
C37Arming an SC seatNoteThe crew list judges each man against that shift's hours only.

Leave, downchits and inputs

CodeCheckLevelWhen it shows
C38An input closes its hoursNoteEvery input closes the man for the hours it covers, from the moment it is filed. One a scheduler has taken off the programme closes nothing.
C39On leave + plannedWarningA man on leave is planned for a flight, sim, duty or ground slot.
C40Downchit + plannedWarningA medically down man is planned. On ATT B he may still stand a duty, sim or ground slot, but not fly.
C41Conflict with a requestWarningAny other input conflicts with a planned slot: a course, a meeting, an appointment, overseas duty.
C42A seat with no timesNoteStill checked against an absence covering the whole day; a part-day absence waits until the seat has times.
C43Half daysNoteLeave and medical can be AM (to 12:00), PM (from 12:01) or all day, and a half day closes only its own half. A sortie counts from its step (Step before take-off), so AM leave still conflicts with a wave that steps before noon.
C44Standing SC SPARENoteA man on local leave may still stand SC SPARE. Overseas leave or duty (OL, OD) or a medical code (HL, OML, ATT C, ATT B) may not: that is a warning. A row that flies has no such allowance.
C45SANS availability — planned outside the availability filedAdvisoryA SANS man planned outside the event or the hours he filed. Filing nothing raises nothing.
C46LATENoteAn input last changed after its cut-off (Inputs late cut-off) wears LATE: a mark, never a warning. Downchits never do.

OIL

CodeCheckLevelWhen it shows
C47Weekend and holiday work earns OILNoteWork on a weekend or public holiday earns OIL once the day is published: a full day or a half, by Full day of OIL.
How it works
  • Weekend or holiday work earns OIL once the day is published.
  • A man's day runs from his first report to his last end, gaps included: 6h01 or more is a full day (FO), less is a half (HO).
  • A flight runs from its in-time or rally, whichever is earlier (Default rally before take-off where neither is entered), to landing plus the debrief. With no landing typed, it lands at its assumed landing (A flight).
  • Any other row the scheduler adds with no times, or no end time, earns nothing, but a request answered yes earns over its own times. An Off day earns nothing.
  • SC SPARE, AVALON and BB rows that do not fly earn only if switched on in OIL Earn. A row that flies earns by default, from its B or R if earlier than its START, otherwise from its START, to its END.
  • Until its wave flies, a desk made from an AVALON or BB template earns only if switched on in OIL Earn. Once the wave flies, the desk earns by default.
  • A Duty & commitments input earns once its OIL question is answered yes.
  • A published day keeps its OIL until it is published again.
C48No OIL earned — a row has no usable timesWarningOn a weekend or holiday, a row with someone on it and no usable times earns nobody on it any OIL. The warning names the row.
C49OIL waiting — this day is not publishedAdvisoryA weekend or holiday with someone to earn is not published yet. Nobody earns until it is.
C50No OIL — no Leave War period covers this dateAdvisoryNo Leave War period covers this weekend or holiday, so its work earns nobody OIL. The day offers to create the period, before and after it is published.
C51Became a holiday after publishing — republish for its OILAdvisoryA day published as a working day that the Leave War now calls a public holiday earns nothing until it is published again.
C52No longer a holiday — republish to withdraw its OILAdvisoryA day published as a holiday that the Leave War no longer calls one keeps its OIL until it is published again, which withdraws it.
C53Published before these seats counted — republish to credit themAdvisoryA weekend or holiday published before the app counted an ALL AVAIL on a duty desk, sim or extra people line shows a pending change. Publish it again and the men behind that puck get their OIL.

7. Standby how SC MAIN, SC SPARE, AVALON and BB are flagged

A standby line is planned like a flying line, with a row for each crew, and each row is MAIN or SPARE. An SC MAIN is checked in full. SC SPARE, AVALON and BB are checked more lightly, because the crew is waiting, not flying. The moment a row flies, it is checked as a sortie.

Swipe the table sideways for SC SPARE, AVALON and BB.

HoursExactly the START and END written. No step, dekit, brief or debrief is added.The same. Overnight.The same. Times are yours to set.
Also down for something else in those hoursFlagged. Red against a flight, a sim, a duty post or another shift. Amber against a ground event or a programme item. Each of the six can be set red or amber (S18).Not flagged, unless it is another SC seat or the SC desk.Not flagged, unless it is another AVALON seat or the AVALON desk.Not flagged, unless it is another seat or the BB desk.
Leave, medical and other inputsFlagged red, as on a flying line, ATT B included. A meeting is amber (C6).Only overseas leave, overseas duty or a medical code is flagged. Local leave and other local inputs may still stand SPARE.Only overseas or medically down is flagged.
CurrencySC DAY if the shift sits wholly inside the SC day window (S17). SC NIGHT if it reaches outside it.SC NIGHT.SC currency for the hours typed.
Front seatPilots only, on all four.
Crew restChecked, measured to the shift's START. Typing its B or R makes the line fly (below), and its crew rest then counts to the B or R.None while standing by.
OIL on a weekend or holidayEarned over its written hours.Only if switched on for that row in OIL Earn.

When a standby line flies

How the app knowsType the line's B or R and every row on it flies. Or tick FLIES on one row on the Scheduler Board and that row flies on its own.
What changesA row that flies has its conflicts and turns checked as a sortie's are, carries crew rest, counts as a jet and a sortie, and earns OIL by default. The SPARE's local-leave allowance no longer applies.
Empty or cancelled rowsA row with nobody on it counts nothing. A row that does not come in is cancelled with CX.
No START or ENDAn advisory says its crew rest and OIL cannot be worked out (C35).

The app's own lines for these are C30 to C37, with C28, C6 and C44.

9. Words that switch a rule on

Most boxes are free text. A few words are read by the app.

You typeWhereWhat happens
AAR DAAR NAARA line's remarksChecks the front seat's refuelling currency. Plain AAR means night on a night wave, day otherwise. NO AAR cancels it.
IRTThe mission, or one aircraft's remarksNeeds an IR examiner in that formation, or in that aircraft.
LATE SHOW SHOW AT BRIEFA line's remarksChanges only how the crew-rest ring is drawn: dashed while the crew can still make step, solid after. The warning stays.
1A: 1B:A line's remarksSays which seat a refuelling remark (AAR) is about: A the front seat, B the back seat. Text with no tag counts as the front seat. No other rule reads it.
0900 IN TIMEThe in-time line above a waveSets the in-time for the whole wave. With a formation's name in it, for that formation only.
EPAn OFT sim row's labelThat sim gets a brief before it and a debrief after it.
BRIEF DEBRIEFAn AMT sim row's labelThat row is the block's brief, or its debrief.
BRIEF 30An OFT sim row's remarksSets that sim's brief to 30 minutes before it.
CXA button on the lineCancels the line and asks why. The line prints "CX DUE" and the reason.

10. What is built around the F-15

These are the places we expect another squadron to differ. Tell us where we are wrong.

TodayFor you?
Two seats on every line. A front seat and a back seat. People are pilots or WSOs, and the seat checks (C19, C24) follow from that.A line with only its front seat filled is planned to work in full for single-seat jets. It is not built yet, and the rules a single-seat squadron needs are not written yet. Your answers decide them.
Crew pairing by category. OCU and CAT A to D decide who may fly with whom, and when an instructor or approval is needed (C20 to C23).What decides it for you?
Three kinds of standby: SC, AVALON and BB, with MAIN and SPARE rows. An SC MAIN is checked in full; SC SPARE, AVALON and BB are checked more lightly, unless they fly (section 7).Which do you hold, and what may a person on standby also do?
Qualification columns: SANS, SXO, Management, Scheduler, SC DAY, SC NIGHT, DAAR, NAAR, NVG, IMC, TF. The warnings read SC DAY, SC NIGHT, DAAR and NAAR (C26 to C28). SANS decides who is checked against SANS availability (C45), and Scheduler who may sign a day. The others are records only.Which currencies should stop or flag a seat for you?
The numbers in section 5 are one squadron's.Each squadron having its own schedule, its own numbers and its own public holidays in the one app is being built now.

11. Questions for you

Short answers are fine. Reply with the question number.

  1. Which numbers in section 5 are different for you, and what is your value?
    These are the times the checks measure with: crew rest, brief, step, dekit, debrief, tight turn, days in a row. Reply by code, for example "S6: 45 min". If a number changes by the kind of sortie or the time of day, say so.
  2. Which checks in section 6 do not apply to you, or work differently?
    Reply by code, for example "C22: does not apply" or "C12: for us this is red, not amber". A check that fires when it should not is as bad as one that is missing.
  3. Which rules or directives do you look up by hand when you plan, that the app should flag for you?
    This is the main one. One line a rule: who it applies to, the limit, and whether breaking it should be red (a rule broken) or amber (worth a look). The aim is that you no longer open the document: the app flags it.
  4. Which of your jets are single-seat and which are two-seat, and who may sit in the back seat of a two-seater?
    Every line today has a front seat and a back seat, and several checks are about the back-seater. Single-seat lines are planned but not built yet, and their rules are not written.
  5. What decides who may fly with whom, or lead whom, in your squadron?
    Today the app uses the F-15 squadron's categories (OCU, CAT A to D) and instructor qualifications to flag a pairing that is not allowed or needs approval.
  6. Which qualifications or currencies should stop or flag a person for a sortie or a duty?
    Today the warnings read four: SC DAY, SC NIGHT, day refuelling and night refuelling. The SANS tick and the Scheduler tick decide who files SANS availability and who may sign a day. Each squadron can keep its own list of qualifications.
  7. How do your SC MAIN, SC SPARE, AVALON and BB differ from section 7: their hours, who may hold them, and what else a person may do while on one?
    Today an SC MAIN is checked in full. SC SPARE, AVALON and BB are checked more lightly than a flying line unless they fly. Say also if you hold any other standby or duty post the app should know.
  8. How does a flying day run for you, in order, and which of those times do you print on the programme?
    Today a wave's typed times run in-time, rally, brief, take-off, landing, and the app flags any typed out of that order. Step, dekit and debrief are not typed: the app works them out from take-off and landing (S6 to S8). It measures crew rest and the working day from all of these.
  9. For training: how do you track a student's or an upgrade's progress today, and what should a scheduler see about it while planning?
    Today the Tracker holds each student's syllabus chart and marks, and the schedule flags crew pairings by category. Tell us what a training appointment holder checks by hand before a sortie is planned.
  10. What does your printed programme show that this one does not?
    Anything: a column, a mark, a note at the foot, a colour that means something.
  11. Can you share one real week of your programme, in any format?
    Seeing a real week answers most of the above faster than any list of questions.
